items.quote: Since 1913, the number of voting representatives has been at 435
items.note: Fixed at 435 by the Reapportionment Act of 1929 (437 briefly 1959-63). 'Voting seats' correctly excludes the six non-voting delegates.

items.quote: Members of the House serve a fixed term of two years, with each seat up for election before the start of the next Congress.
The drive to lower the voting age from 21 to 18 grew across the country during the 1960s
items.note: Strictly the amendment bars denying the vote to citizens 18 and over rather than 'lowering' an age, but the wording is the common shorthand and the answer is unambiguous.

items.quote: The terms are staggered so that approximately one-third of the seats are up for election every two years.
items.note: 'Roughly' in the question matches 'approximately' (33 or 34 seats of 100).

items.quote: A candidate must receive an absolute majority of electoral votes (currently 270) to win the presidency or the vice presidency.
On the 100th anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment
items.note: Content confirmed by the same article's lead: 'prohibits the United States and its states from denying the right to vote to citizens of the United States on the basis of sex'. Ratified August 1920.

items.quote: Each representative must: (1) be at least twenty-five (25) years old
seats in the House of Representatives are apportioned among the states by population, as determined by the census conducted every ten years
Because the 17th Amendment vests the power to grant that authority to the legislature
items.note: This quote only ties the numeral to the amendment. Content confirmed by en:Seventeenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution lead: 'established the direct election of United States senators in each state', and by en:United_States_Senate: 'Before the adoption of the Seventeenth Amendment in 1913, senators were elected by the individual state legislatures.'

items.quote: Congress responded in 1845 by mandating a uniform national date for choosing Presidential electors.
items.note: en:Presidential_Election_Day_Act: 'On January 23, 1845, the 28th US Congress passed "An act to establish a uniform time for holding elections for electors of President and Vice President in all the States of the Union." The act selected "the Tuesday after the first Monday in November"'. The question correctly says presidential ELECTORS (the House date came later, in 1872), so 1872 is not a competing answer. Hard but fair as a closer.
